beats.text: A D H D me. The front door to A D H D care in Australia.
Getting A D H D care in Australia is a maze.
The cost is hidden until after you have paid, and waited.
You get whoever is available. Not whoever fits.
And every clinician assesses you differently.
When care is handed over, prescriptions lapse without warning.
So people give up before the first booking.
We start with sixteen to twenty-five year olds in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane. People seeking a diagnosis, or finding their way after one.
A D H D me is matching, not triage. Not the next free slot. The right person.
A new parent in the postpartum period is matched with a G P who has perinatal experience.
Someone from a South Asian family, where A D H D is not talked about at home, is matched with a doctor who shares that background and speaks Hindi and Urdu.
Someone afraid of being judged for wanting medication is matched with a clinician who uses plain language, and no judgement.
Postpartum. Cultural background. Stigma. The things a directory never asks.
Costs are published as bands before you book. And A D H D me is free for patients.
Standard diagnosis templates mean the same assessment from every clinician.
And script expiry alerts mean no lapse at handover.
Why now? G Ps can now diagnose A D H D. Queensland went live in December twenty twenty-five. New South Wales and Victoria follow through twenty twenty-six.
More than a million Australians have A D H D. A quarter of a million are actively seeking care.
It is free for patients. Clinicians subscribe for a steady flow of well matched patients.
We are live today at A D H D me dot A U, with two G Ps in Sydney, and two matching models in test.
The right A D H D doctor should not be hard to find.
A D H D me.
